evidence: The PR renamed scout→workers to partition→workers in README and src/run.js but a1585ee's diff shows src/failover.js still read 'the whole scout->workers pass' and 'an entire scout→workers pass' until the fix; the stale prose was real and the fix updated both sites.
guidance_note: When renaming a concept across docs, grep the old term repo-wide (including the module that owns the documented math) before pushing, not just the files already being edited.

guidance_note: When deleting a function that reconciled a value (planScopes), list every diagnostic it emitted and confirm each has a successor in the replacement checkpoint before pushing.

guidance_note: When a fix adds a new refusal reason, grep for every doc and help text that enumerates the existing reasons (here 'both directions' / 'omits') and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The garbled 'scoutUsage is what deciding cost' is an added line in the original PR hunk, not from a review fix (the 920bc8c flag only marks the head commit, which touched partition.js); 5c1e4a0 changes it to 'what deciding it cost'.

guidance_note: When a change removes a property (scout nondeterminism) that a doc claim depends on, re-read every paragraph you edit in full for claims that relied on the old property, not just the sentence you changed.

guidance_note: When fixing a stale enumeration in one doc, grep the distinctive phrasing ('omits', 'diff lacks') across help text and comments and fix every copy in the same commit.

evidence: The code matched its own comment ('keys on the directory of the ONE changed source whose stem it names'), and a suffix-less test/config.js may well test src/config.js, so the claimed misgrouping is a heuristic preference rather than a clear bug; the packet shows no case deciding which grouping is better. Original PR code, so the e7f4d52 flag is a false positive.

isTestPath checked only `p.split('/')[0]` against TEST_DIRS, so src/components/__tests__/Button.js was not recognised as a test despite the comment saying tests are recognised 'by where they live'; original PR code, flag e7f4d52 is a false positive.
guidance_note: When writing a path classifier, list the accepted shapes (top-level test dir, nested __tests__, monorepo packages/x/test) as test cases before writing the predicate.

narrative: A large refactor replacing the LLM scout with a deterministic partition for PR mode. Most findings were in the original PR's own code or prose (stale 'scout' terminology, the 'scout missing' footer that the posted reviews themselves displayed, partition heuristics). The one fix-caused chain is F2's new duplicate-claim refusal, which drifted from the README (F4) and then the run-case.js help text (F8) because each fix updated only one enumeration of the refusal reasons. Every round also carried non-caused findings, so no round was avoidable; round 5 was the round-cap no-op.
guidance_observations: The agent accepted every finding without pushback; nine of ten were real, and F9 was a heuristic preference that it accepted without weighing it.
Terminology renames (scout→partition) produced findings in rounds 0, 0-outside-diff, and 3-outside-diff; one repo-wide grep for 'scout' at authoring time would have caught them all.
When a fix adds a new case to an enumerated rule, grepping for every place that enumerates the old cases would have closed the F2→F4→F8 chain in one commit.
